title: Ishigaki vs Miyako: Which Okinawan Island Should You Visit?
verdict: Ishigaki for diverse activities, island-hopping, and food variety. Miyako for Japan's best beaches, quiet luxury, and world-class diving visibility. Both run ~¥12,000–18,000/day mid-range. Do both if you have 5+ days.

categories.name: Beaches & Swimming
categories.summary: Miyako's Yonaha Maehama is Japan's #1 beach. Crystal-clear turquoise water across multiple world-class stretches. Ishigaki's Kabira Bay is stunning but doesn't allow swimming.

categories.name: Snorkeling & Diving
categories.summary: Ishigaki for manta rays at Manta Scramble (world-class). Miyako for 30m+ visibility and spectacular cave dives. Both excellent for shore snorkeling.

categories.name: Cost Comparison
categories.summary: Nearly identical daily costs: ¥12,000–18,000 ($80–120) mid-range. Ishigaki has more budget options; Miyako's resorts are pricier.

categories.name: Getting There
categories.summary: Both have direct flights from Tokyo (~3h), Osaka (~2.5h), Naha (~1h). 35-minute direct flight between the two islands.

categories.name: Getting Around
categories.summary: Miyako's flat terrain makes cycling viable and enjoyable. Ishigaki is hilly and requires a rental car.

categories.name: Food & Dining
categories.summary: Ishigaki wins for variety: wagyu-grade Ishigaki beef, yaeyama soba, lively izakaya scene. Miyako has Miyako soba and fresh seafood but fewer options.

categories.name: Best Time to Visit
categories.summary: Both: March–May and Oct–Nov best. Avoid Aug–Sep typhoon peak. Ishigaki has whale shark season April–June.

categories.name: Where to Stay
categories.summary: Budget travelers: Ishigaki downtown. Luxury/romance: Miyako's Shigira resort area. Both have solid mid-range options.

categories.name: Day Trips & Activities
categories.summary: Ishigaki is gateway to Iriomote (jungle), Taketomi (traditional village), and more Yaeyama islands. Miyako has bridge-connected islands but less variety.

categories.name: Why Not Both?
categories.summary: 35-minute flight apart. 3 days each is ideal. Fly into one, out of the other to avoid backtracking.

faq.question: Which island has better beaches — Ishigaki or Miyako?
faq.answer: Miyako wins. Yonaha Maehama is ranked Japan's #1 beach. Ishigaki's Kabira Bay is beautiful but doesn't allow swimming.

faq.question: Can you visit both Ishigaki and Miyako on one trip?
faq.answer: Yes — 35-minute direct flights connect them. Most travelers recommend 3 days on each island.

faq.question: When is the best time to visit?
faq.answer: March–May and late October–November. Avoid August–September typhoon peak. Whale sharks near Ishigaki April–June.

faq.question: Which is better for snorkeling/diving?
faq.answer: Ishigaki for manta rays (Manta Scramble). Miyako for crystal-clear visibility (30m+) and cave dives. Both world-class.

faq.question: How do you get between Ishigaki and Miyako?
faq.answer: Direct flights (~35min, ¥8,000–15,000). No regular public ferry — must fly or connect via Naha.

faq.question: Which island is better for families?
faq.answer: Ishigaki has more varied activities (glass-bottom boats, Taketomi buffalo carts). Miyako has calmer beaches for swimming and flat cycling.

faq.question: Is Ishigaki or Miyako more expensive?
faq.answer: Very similar. Budget ¥8,000–10,000/night, mid-range ¥15,000–25,000. Ishigaki has more budget options; Miyako's resorts are pricier.

faq.question: Which island has better food?
faq.answer: Ishigaki — more restaurants, Ishigaki beef (wagyu-grade), yaeyama soba, lively izakaya scene. Miyako has Miyako soba but fewer options.
